insights: Selberg sieve gives condition (1) (large prime factors) but NOT condition (2) (composite subtractions)
Key obstruction: if n has all prime factors > l, no small prime q <= l can divide n, blocking the standard composite-certification approach
Condition (2) likely requires CRT-based sieve: choose n in progressions that force n-k! divisible by specific large primes
factorial_interval_size proof: use Nat.succ_mul + Nat.add_sub_cancel_right (not omega — products of variables)
prime_gt_not_dvd_factorial: prove by induction, using Nat.Prime.dvd_mul in succ case
nextSteps: Prove coprime_of_large_factors_lt: needs Nat.exists_prime_and_dvd + prime divisors of factorial are small
Formalize the CRT-based compositeness argument if possible
Consider Aristotle for coprime_of_large_factors_lt (routine Mathlib proof)
